All 68 World Heritage properties in Spain, Portugal, Andorra and Gibraltar are tagged — 62 matched to existing Lonely Planet rows, 6 added as rows of their own — and 28 of the 47 tentative-list entries are represented, marked WHS-T. None of the four territories has ever had a property delisted, so there is no former-site category. Tags for large serial and urban properties are applied at destination level: every attraction inside the inscribed area carries the tag. Spain is grouped by its 17 autonomous communities and Portugal by its seven regions; Ceuta and Melilla have no Lonely Planet attractions. Sources: Lonely Planet’s points-of-interest index, the UNESCO World Heritage List and English Wikipedia. Founding dates come from Wikidata and from the opening paragraph of each Wikipedia article; rows with no article of their own are dated by site type, which is an estimate rather than a source. Where the Moorish and Christian bands overlap, the era is resolved by an explicit marker in the name first, then by the reconquest date of that region. Map links are searches, not pins: Lonely Planet publishes no coordinates.
